title: Rewriting Shine and the song Darling
summary: He wrote the new lyrics to Shine, was paid only for his act, and turned the idea into a song called Darling.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You did say that you wrote that piece of music.
That's what you call a reprieve of 'Shine.' I wrote the lyrics that I put into that 'Shine.'
No. Somebody else wrote 'Shine,' but I don't know who wrote it. I forgot the man's name who wrote it. I got a clipping about who wrote it, but I forgot what I did with it.
And they didn't pay you for doing that?
No. They paid me for doing my act, for the time I used in doing the number, but I wanted to be the one to worry about what I'm going to do in this

show, in the thing. I want to worry about how-----me start standing out. Oh, in that picture -- what did I write -- was it that picture -- and I took that song from that I wrote another song called "Darling." And they recorded it. They had 15 violins playing the verse and it was like,

"Darling you are mighty fine A gift sent from above It must have been your mommy and your dad Lønging for someone to love And it's very plain to see Just how it happened to be I met your mommy in a cafe It was on a Sunday in the eve When I saw her and she looked at me We were very pleased I never knew then that I loved her And by all the stars above There's no one in all this world But you I trust to love."

That was what I took from that "Shine" and made another song out of it for the girl that I thought I was going to have in my future days. What else did I want to tell you about it? Can't think of what else I can tell. You got some questions you want to ask me to tell about?
